title: Half the bytes, exactly merged
subtitle: The INT8 history format and the SYCL attention kernels that halve ActiveKV's bus traffic, and the log-sum-exp merge that keeps the result exact

lede: Once a model's attention history lives in host memory, decode speed is bus arithmetic. The model ActiveKV serves carries 64 KiB of key-value history per token across its sixteen dense layers, and the exact path re-reads all of it for every generated token: 2.1 GB at 32K tokens, 8.4 GB at 128K, across a copy engine that moves about 26 GB per second. A calibrated model of that arithmetic matched measured latency within a few percent at every context length. So the way to make long contexts faster was to move fewer bytes without changing the answer.
quote: Averaging those outputs would be wrong, because each is normalised by a different denominator.
evidence: LLM quantization (INT8 KV cache): a compressed history format with eight-bit codes and separable key scales, worst merged own-format error 0.00267 against a 0.005 gate.
SYCL kernel development on Intel Xe2: integer query-key attention on the matrix units, from 18.69 to 8.74 ms per prefill tile, nine percent faster than BF16.
Exact attention merging: partial attention across tiles and precisions combined through log-sum-exp weights with no approximation, 12 of 12 bitwise cells on the hybrid route.
KV-cache offload for LLM inference: per-token latency at 128K tokens cut from 335.2 ms on the exact tier to 190.0 ms on the hybrid tier.
GPU inference optimisation: one decode launch serving two requests 31% faster than two single calls, and one-row compressed decode 26% faster than BF16.
author: Corey James
